transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

I’m here because… there’s been trouble with my husband’s sister. I don’t really want to get into all of it right away, but she’s been working things in the family business so she can get control of the money and leave me out of decisions. People keep trying to make it sound harmless, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been going on over a year.
Besides your concerns about your sister-in-law, have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t been seeing things or hearing voices, if that’s what you mean.
Aside from your sister-in-law, do you generally find yourself distrusting or suspecting the motives of other people in your life, like friends, coworkers, or other family members?
Not really… I mean, I don’t go around suspecting everybody. I keep to myself mostly. This is… it’s more about her and what’s been happening there.

Apart from this situation with your sister-in-law, has your day-to-day life—like your work, taking care of yourself, or your relationships with others—been affected or harder to manage over this past year?

No, not really. I still do my quilting group, choir practice… my GED lessons, and the walks with the seniors. I take care of my things. It’s mostly just changed how I deal with his sister, and which family gatherings I feel okay going to.
Have you noticed any changes in how your thoughts flow, like feeling like your thinking is jumbled or that others might have trouble following what you're saying?
I don’t think so… I mean, nobody’s told me they can’t follow me. My thoughts feel pretty normal to me.

latest_inference.note: Functioning remains intact across multiple domains (quilting, choir, GED classes, volunteering), and the belief is a single, circumscribed, non-bizarre delusion about the sister-in-law without generalized suspiciousness, hallucinations, or disorganized thought. This pattern fits delusional disorder (F22) better than unspecified psychosis (F28), which is ruled out given the clear, persistent, circumscribed delusional theme lasting over a year.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusion of a persecutory/jealous-financial nature involving her sister-in-law, persisting for over a year. There are no hallucinations, no evidence of disorganized thought process, and no broader pattern of pervasive distrust or suspiciousness toward others (ruling out paranoid personality disorder). Functioning outside the delusional theme remains intact (continues quilting, choir, GED classes, volunteer walks), which argues against schizophrenia (F20) given the absence of negative symptoms, hallucinations, disorganization, or global functional decline. The circumscribed, encapsulated nature of the delusion with preserved functioning and behavior is most consistent with delusional disorder.
